newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Bank to issue T$6.8 bln Taiwan-dollar bond in May.
newsitem.headline: Bank to issue T$6.8 bln Taiwan-dollar bond in May.

text.p: The Central American Bank of Economic Integration planned to issue T$6.8 billion (US$240 million) worth of Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in May, lead underwriter Citibank of Taiwan said on Wednesday.
The issue would have a five-year term and a coupon rate of roughly 7.55 percent, a Citibank spokesman said by telephone.
"We will hold an information seminar on Friday to reveal more details on the issue," the spokesman said.
Other underwriters for the issue included International Commercial Bank of China and Bank of Taiwan, he said.
He declined to give other details on the issue.
The Central American Bank of Economic Integration, based in Honduras, would become the second development bank to issue Taiwan dollar bonds.
The Asian Development Bank issued T$2.6 billion (US$100 million) worth of Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds in August 1995, and a T$7 billion (US$255 million) issue in December 1996.
Analysts have said the issues reflected a drive by Taiwan's government to encourage international agencies to raise capital in the island's cash-flush money market.
